Call/Text Us Now

You deserve to enjoy the wonderful feeling of coming home to a loyal companion. At Blackberry Farm Puppies, we are passionate and excited about sharing our love of dogs with you. When you decide to adopt a puppy, many questions can quickly arise. Let our friendly staff put your mind at ease as you shop for a new and loving member of the family.

When you browse our available Bernedoodle puppies, you can find your new best friend that will love you and stay by your side for countless years to come. We take the important and necessary steps to ensure your new Bernedoodle puppy is happy, healthy, and ready to come home with you. Bring home an adorable new member of the family today when you decide to adopt a Bernedoodle with us.

Browse Our Available Bernedoodles

When you are looking to adopt a puppy, it’s important to consider the environment of your home and your current lifestyle. Thankfully, Bernedoodles make stellar companions with their loving and friendly nature. Bernedoodles are intelligent, loyal, and family-friendly. Additionally, Bernedoodles are low- to non-shedding dogs, which can free your home of bothersome allergies.

We are happily providing Bernedoodle puppies throughout Utah, California, and across the United States. When you decide to adopt a Bernedoodle through Blackberry Farm Puppies, you can have the confidence of knowing you are working with a family that is committed to the health and safety of our dogs.

Our Bernedoodle puppies are ready to find their loving home and start creating lasting memories with your family. If you are ready to see our available Bernedoodle puppies and find the perfect match for you, read on to take a look at our beautiful dogs. Visit our about us page today. For any general questions about the adoption process, contact us through our home page.

pages.title: About Us
pages.heading: Who I Am
pages.body:
Who I Am

Hi! I’m Melissa. We have a wonderful family business where we responsibly raise happy, healthy, well-socialized puppies with the help of my sister and her family, my 2 daughters, my daughter in law, and some amazing guardian homes. We live on a beautiful fruit farm where we grow cherries, grapes, pears, apples, plums, peaches, nectarines, mulberries and of course blackberries. We have always loved working outside with a big yard and having our dogs there to help us and enjoy all the adventures that a big yard has to offer. Raising them in our home over the years has been one of our greatest joys!

At Blackberry Farm Puppies, we raise exceptional animals in a loving and caring environment according to a responsible breeding program. Some of our happiest moments are when our puppies are adopted by loving families. We currently raise a variety of hypoallergenic poodle mixes and purebreds with a specialty in Bernedoodles and Cavapoos.

## Commitment to Responsible Breeding We raise our puppies in our home. They are part of our family from the first day they are born. Our dogs are my full-time job, and my top priority is ensuring that each of our dogs and puppies is safe and healthy. Our responsibility is to provide the best possible start and a wide array of socialization skills that will be a long life foundation for each puppy and be able to promote the best possible temperament and socially sound puppies. We practice ENS (Early Neurological Stimulation) with our puppies. Some of the benefits of ENS include greater resistance to disease, more tolerance to stress, and a stronger heartbeat, just to name a few. We spend many hours with each puppy.

Here are a few things we do with them:

  • Daily activities to shape temperament
  • Multiple de-worming at appropriate ages
  • Positive socialization with children, men, women, and our other dogs
  • Car rides
  • Noise desensitization
  • Potty training started
  • Bathing and brushing
  • Trimming their nails
  • Clipper desensitization
  • And much more
Our dogs have been genetic tested through Embark or Animal Genetics. While this doesn’t guarantee that nothing will ever go wrong with your dogs health, it allows us to avoid passing on known preventable diseases. Our objective is to produce healthy, happy puppies, and this is a great start to doing so.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

faqs.question: How often do I feed my puppy?
faqs.answer:
We free feed our puppies, meaning we leave food and water out for them all day and just take it away about an hour before bed time. They are not used to eating a lot at once. They just eat a little at a time all throughout the day.

You can do this or ask your vet what he or she recommends.

faqs.question: What is my puppy used to sleeping in?
faqs.answer:
We suggest purchasing a puppy gate from a pet store that is about as high up as your waist. You can put this in your kitchen area or anywhere you have hard surface flooring, that’s easy to clean.

You can place a food and water dish, blanket to sleep on, toys, and some pee pads at the back. This is a perfect place to contain your puppy when you have to leave or unable to watch them closely until he/she is completely potty trained!

You can also put a crate in there with the door left open if you’d like.

faqs.question: What is the best way to travel back home with my puppy?
faqs.answer:
Your little one will most likely want to be on someone’s lap on the way home. But if he/she gets restless, and needs to go potty, we recommend bringing a large/medium plastic storage container (like what you’d store Christmas decorations in) with pee pads in the bottom. You can put your puppy right in there to potty. And as soon as he/she is done, I’m sure he/she will want right back out to sit on your lap again. It’s works really slick!

Bring some paper towels and some small bags you can put the soiled pee pad in, and throw away.

Do NOT put your puppy down on the ground anywhere but in your own yard. Not even in a parking lot or side of the road. Do NOT set him/her down anywhere. They are not fully vaccinated at this point and the Parvo virus is so deadly to little puppies. They will need all their shots before they can be let down anywhere other than your yard. The virus can live in the ground for up to two years. So please don’t take that risk!

They should be done with their shots at 16 weeks of age, or soon after that. They need a shot every 3-4 weeks. Not sooner than 3 weeks from the last shot and not later than 4.

faqs.question: Will my puppy be started on crate training?
faqs.answer:
No! We do not crate train our puppies. Our puppies live in our home in fenced off areas. We expand their areas as they grow and need more room to play. They sleep all together in a big dog pile.

I’d suggest searching the internet for ideas on how to crate train your puppy if you choose to do that.

faqs.question: What is the best brush to use on my puppy?
faqs.answer:
Chris Christiensen Big G Slicker Brush. Being a hair dresser for many years, I have researched and tried out at least 30 different dog brushes and combs to brush out these sweet fur babies. I finally found one that works amazingly well and will last you years! It’s pricey but well worth purchasing one. It will be the only brush you’ll ever need!

A metal comb is also nice to have for their little faces and places it’s hard to brush!

We love the Dirty Dog shampoo. It works great and has a great smell that lasts for several days.

Keep the hair trimmed up around their potty area to keep them cleaner! You can get a tiny trimmer or just use scissors to keep the hair short! They can’t clean themselves very well when the hair is really thick down there. :)

pages.title: Preparing Our Puppies
pages.heading: Preparing Our Puppies
pages.body:
HEALTH GUARANTEE

When you take your four-legged friend home, he or she comes with a one-year health guarantee, and a spay/neuter contract. We deworm each puppy at two, four, six, and eight weeks old. When the puppies are 7-8 weeks old, we will take them to our vet for their first set of puppy shots, and checked out from head to toe. We have their dewclaws removed within the first five days of life so it doesn't get caught on something, ripped, and infected later on. All our puppies are fed the Costco Nature's Domain Chicken and Pea puppy kibble and nursed several times each day.

We also start potty training our puppies at three weeks old, and we provide the best possible start and wide array of socialization skills that will be a life foundation for each puppy and be able to promote the best possible temperament and socially sound puppy for you. When it’s time to pick him or her up, your fur baby will be bright-eyed, bushy-tailed, and ready to love you!

What we will be sending home with your fur baby:

  • Vet vaccination and deworming records.
  • Nail clippers. Small ones for now, larger ones for later. We suggest pretending to cut their nails often as this will make cutting their nails a breeze in the future.
  • A couple toys.
  • Blanket that smells like momma and the puppy's siblings.
  • Leash and collar. No need to buy an expensive collar right now as your puppy grows so quickly.
  • Sales contract/Health guarantee.
  • A small baggy of the puppy food that your little one has been eating (Nature's Domain Puppy Chicken and Pea Formula). It won't last long, but it is enough to get you through the ride home if you have a long drive or if you didn't get to the store to pick up a bag of their food yet. If you prefer to feed your fur baby a different kind of puppy food, get at least one bag of Nature's Domain and mix it half-and-half with the puppy food you prefer so your fur baby's stomach has enough time to get used to the new kind of puppy food. You'll need to feed your fur baby puppy food for a full year! A good rule of thumb when choosing a dog or puppy food is to make sure that the first two ingredients do not contain any kind of "meal." So try to avoid chicken meal, beef meal, fish meal, etc. "Meal" is the waste material such as organs, blood, bones, and feathers of the animal or fish that is from slaughterhouses that is processed and not fit for human consumption.
  • Pee pads (a few to get you home).

pages.title: Shipping Options
pages.heading: Shipping and Delivery Options
pages.body:
We are located in Utah, but we proudly work with families across all 50 states to make bringing home your puppy as smooth and stress-free as possible.

## 🚗 Personal Delivery to Southern California

We travel to Southern California nearly every other weekend to personally deliver puppies to their new families. This option allows us to meet you in person, answer any questions, and ensure your puppy has a safe, comfortable trip. The delivery cost for this service is $200.

## ✈️ Flight Nanny Service (Nationwide)

For families outside of driving distance, we work with a trusted and experienced flight nanny who accompanies your puppy in-cabin on a commercial flight. We rarely ship puppies in the cargo area. The flight nanny stays with your puppy the entire journey and personally hands them to you at the airport. This option is safe, reliable, and allows puppies to travel comfortably to families all over the U.S. The Flight Nanny service has varying rates depending on location, but we are happy to get a quote for you.

docs.title: About Us
docs.heading: Who I Am
docs.body:
Who I Am

Hi! I’m Melissa. We have a wonderful family business where we responsibly raise happy, healthy, well-socialized puppies with the help of my sister and her family, my 2 daughters, my daughter in law, and some amazing guardian homes. We live on a beautiful fruit farm where we grow cherries, grapes, pears, apples, plums, peaches, nectarines, mulberries and of course blackberries. We have always loved working outside with a big yard and having our dogs there to help us and enjoy all the adventures that a big yard has to offer. Raising them in our home over the years has been one of our greatest joys!

At Blackberry Farm Puppies, we raise exceptional animals in a loving and caring environment according to a responsible breeding program. Some of our happiest moments are when our puppies are adopted by loving families. We currently raise a variety of hypoallergenic poodle mixes and purebreds with a specialty in Bernedoodles and Cavapoos.

## Commitment to Responsible Breeding We raise our puppies in our home. They are part of our family from the first day they are born. Our dogs are my full-time job, and my top priority is ensuring that each of our dogs and puppies is safe and healthy. Our responsibility is to provide the best possible start and a wide array of socialization skills that will be a long life foundation for each puppy and be able to promote the best possible temperament and socially sound puppies. We practice ENS (Early Neurological Stimulation) with our puppies. Some of the benefits of ENS include greater resistance to disease, more tolerance to stress, and a stronger heartbeat, just to name a few. We spend many hours with each puppy.

Here are a few things we do with them:

  • Daily activities to shape temperament
  • Multiple de-worming at appropriate ages
  • Positive socialization with children, men, women, and our other dogs
  • Car rides
  • Noise desensitization
  • Potty training started
  • Bathing and brushing
  • Trimming their nails
  • Clipper desensitization
  • And much more
Our dogs have been genetic tested through Embark or Animal Genetics. While this doesn’t guarantee that nothing will ever go wrong with your dogs health, it allows us to avoid passing on known preventable diseases. Our objective is to produce healthy, happy puppies, and this is a great start to doing so.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

faqs.question: How often do I feed my puppy?
faqs.answer:
We free feed our puppies, meaning we leave food and water out for them all day and just take it away about an hour before bed time. They are not used to eating a lot at once. They just eat a little at a time all throughout the day.

You can do this or ask your vet what he or she recommends.

faqs.question: What is my puppy used to sleeping in?
faqs.answer:
We suggest purchasing a puppy gate from a pet store that is about as high up as your waist. You can put this in your kitchen area or anywhere you have hard surface flooring, that’s easy to clean.

You can place a food and water dish, blanket to sleep on, toys, and some pee pads at the back. This is a perfect place to contain your puppy when you have to leave or unable to watch them closely until he/she is completely potty trained!

You can also put a crate in there with the door left open if you’d like.

faqs.question: What is the best way to travel back home with my puppy?
faqs.answer:
Your little one will most likely want to be on someone’s lap on the way home. But if he/she gets restless, and needs to go potty, we recommend bringing a large/medium plastic storage container (like what you’d store Christmas decorations in) with pee pads in the bottom. You can put your puppy right in there to potty. And as soon as he/she is done, I’m sure he/she will want right back out to sit on your lap again. It’s works really slick!

Bring some paper towels and some small bags you can put the soiled pee pad in, and throw away.

Do NOT put your puppy down on the ground anywhere but in your own yard. Not even in a parking lot or side of the road. Do NOT set him/her down anywhere. They are not fully vaccinated at this point and the Parvo virus is so deadly to little puppies. They will need all their shots before they can be let down anywhere other than your yard. The virus can live in the ground for up to two years. So please don’t take that risk!

They should be done with their shots at 16 weeks of age, or soon after that. They need a shot every 3-4 weeks. Not sooner than 3 weeks from the last shot and not later than 4.

faqs.question: Will my puppy be started on crate training?
faqs.answer:
No! We do not crate train our puppies. Our puppies live in our home in fenced off areas. We expand their areas as they grow and need more room to play. They sleep all together in a big dog pile.

I’d suggest searching the internet for ideas on how to crate train your puppy if you choose to do that.

faqs.question: What is the best brush to use on my puppy?
faqs.answer:
Chris Christiensen Big G Slicker Brush. Being a hair dresser for many years, I have researched and tried out at least 30 different dog brushes and combs to brush out these sweet fur babies. I finally found one that works amazingly well and will last you years! It’s pricey but well worth purchasing one. It will be the only brush you’ll ever need!

A metal comb is also nice to have for their little faces and places it’s hard to brush!

We love the Dirty Dog shampoo. It works great and has a great smell that lasts for several days.

Keep the hair trimmed up around their potty area to keep them cleaner! You can get a tiny trimmer or just use scissors to keep the hair short! They can’t clean themselves very well when the hair is really thick down there. :)

docs.title: Preparing Our Puppies
docs.heading: Preparing Our Puppies
docs.body:
HEALTH GUARANTEE

When you take your four-legged friend home, he or she comes with a one-year health guarantee, and a spay/neuter contract. We deworm each puppy at two, four, six, and eight weeks old. When the puppies are 7-8 weeks old, we will take them to our vet for their first set of puppy shots, and checked out from head to toe. We have their dewclaws removed within the first five days of life so it doesn't get caught on something, ripped, and infected later on. All our puppies are fed the Costco Nature's Domain Chicken and Pea puppy kibble and nursed several times each day.

We also start potty training our puppies at three weeks old, and we provide the best possible start and wide array of socialization skills that will be a life foundation for each puppy and be able to promote the best possible temperament and socially sound puppy for you. When it’s time to pick him or her up, your fur baby will be bright-eyed, bushy-tailed, and ready to love you!

What we will be sending home with your fur baby:

  • Vet vaccination and deworming records.
  • Nail clippers. Small ones for now, larger ones for later. We suggest pretending to cut their nails often as this will make cutting their nails a breeze in the future.
  • A couple toys.
  • Blanket that smells like momma and the puppy's siblings.
  • Leash and collar. No need to buy an expensive collar right now as your puppy grows so quickly.
  • Sales contract/Health guarantee.
  • A small baggy of the puppy food that your little one has been eating (Nature's Domain Puppy Chicken and Pea Formula). It won't last long, but it is enough to get you through the ride home if you have a long drive or if you didn't get to the store to pick up a bag of their food yet. If you prefer to feed your fur baby a different kind of puppy food, get at least one bag of Nature's Domain and mix it half-and-half with the puppy food you prefer so your fur baby's stomach has enough time to get used to the new kind of puppy food. You'll need to feed your fur baby puppy food for a full year! A good rule of thumb when choosing a dog or puppy food is to make sure that the first two ingredients do not contain any kind of "meal." So try to avoid chicken meal, beef meal, fish meal, etc. "Meal" is the waste material such as organs, blood, bones, and feathers of the animal or fish that is from slaughterhouses that is processed and not fit for human consumption.
  • Pee pads (a few to get you home).

docs.title: Shipping Options
docs.heading: Shipping and Delivery Options
docs.body:
We are located in Utah, but we proudly work with families across all 50 states to make bringing home your puppy as smooth and stress-free as possible.

## 🚗 Personal Delivery to Southern California

We travel to Southern California nearly every other weekend to personally deliver puppies to their new families. This option allows us to meet you in person, answer any questions, and ensure your puppy has a safe, comfortable trip. The delivery cost for this service is $200.

## ✈️ Flight Nanny Service (Nationwide)

For families outside of driving distance, we work with a trusted and experienced flight nanny who accompanies your puppy in-cabin on a commercial flight. We rarely ship puppies in the cargo area. The flight nanny stays with your puppy the entire journey and personally hands them to you at the airport. This option is safe, reliable, and allows puppies to travel comfortably to families all over the U.S. The Flight Nanny service has varying rates depending on location, but we are happy to get a quote for you.
